quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for passengers. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is just part of riding a motorcycle

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection while riding. It will protect your hearing and still let you hear important sounds like sirens or car horns.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding to maintain proper balance.

questions.question: If you are in a collision, you must report it to law enforcement if it causes:
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, you must report a collision to authorities if anyone is injured, if someone dies, or if property damage is $1,000 or more.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than you normally would
Start slowing down earlier than you normally would
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than you normally would

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than you normally would
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes your motorcycle respond more slowly to your actions. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. To ride safely with a passenger, reduce your speed, slow down earlier, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: You must have ______ insurance to legally operate a motor vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your license can be suspended if you operate a motor vehicle without liability insurance.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device
Move to the outside edge of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into the part of your lane that other drivers can see as early as possible.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers

questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash, keeps you comfortable, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road splits into separate directions ahead.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcyclists are:
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the best foot protection while riding. Choose boots that are high enough and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locked brakes can cause you to lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again right away. If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you more visible and keeps safe space around you.
Is whatever you like, without thinking about others.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible and keeps safe space around you.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Good riders change position as road conditions change. No single position is always best or always bad.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind.

questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snug enough that they do not flap in the wind. They should not be so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Test that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure the bike is clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test both your front and rear brakes to make sure they turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It makes steering hard, which affects your balance.
It stops the front brake from working.
It keeps you from speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes steering hard, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering hard. This hurts your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Keeps you away from road hazards.
Puts you right next to another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps you away from road hazards.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid hazards on the road. Always keep safe space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Riders use a system called SIPDE to make safe decisions. What does "I" stand for?
questions.explanation: SIPDE stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. This system helps riders make safe choices while riding.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep riding because the danger is past.
Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop and remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: Pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is stuck in the chain or belt before you continue riding.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should a protective jacket do?

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket made of leather or sturdy material. It should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but still allow you to move freely.
